  ref: "kvclcdjmjghndxsngfzb"

| Endpoint | Result |

A real owner token has `role: "authenticated"`, a `sub` (user UUID), and an `email` claim. You get one by **logging into the IVX app** — the app calls Supabase `signInWithPassword`, which returns an `access_token` with those claims.

1. Open the IVX IA app and log in with your owner credentials
2. Run: `rork-agent logs runtime | rg -i "access_token|bearer|session"`
3. Copy the `access_token` value (starts with `eyJ...` and is much longer than the anon key)

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://kvclcdjmjghndxsngfzb.supabase.co/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password" \
  -H "apikey: <ANON_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"iperez4242@gmail.com","password":"<YOUR_PASSWORD>"}'
```

The response will contain `access_token` — that's the real owner session token. Paste it here and I'll run the full autonomous end-to-end test immediately.

**Option C — paste it from the app:**
If you can see the network tab in the app or developer tools, look for any request to `api.ivxholding.com` with an `Authorization: Bearer eyJ...` header — that token is what I need.

---

**Bottom line:** The token you gave me is the public anon key, not a login session. The auth gate is working correctly — it blocked the anon key just as designed. I need your actual logged-in session token to trigger the real autonomous worker.
